evidence.quote: Technique Capability or Protocol applies, invokes, or runs another technique for work, by `Apply [technique]` or a `::` invocation, one or many.
Replace the raw tool name with the canonical hyperlinked wrapping op; preserve arguments.
Name the omitted input at the Apply site. Where the value has no home on the applying technique, declare it there first, then pass it.
a technique that only applies a sibling without listing a parallel set.
Each sibling or shared technique is its own step. A technique Protocol applies tools and resources.

findings.problem: AP-114 and DP-25 place composition on the run, while AP-51/AP-141 repair ordinary Protocol into valid-looking technique invocations. AP-107 explicitly exempts a sibling Apply. These are incompatible remedies and an unstated exception boundary, not proof that no conforming workflow exists.
findings.witness: A local Protocol calls a raw tool with an existing shared wrapper. AP-51 prescribes replacement by a hyperlinked wrapping op with arguments; AP-114 immediately flags that work invocation. Repairing its omitted inputs under AP-141 leaves the AP-114 defect.
findings.proposed_fix: Adopt DP-25 for ordinary techniques: AP-51 binds the wrapper as an activity/routine step; AP-141 checks required inputs at those binding sites; AP-107 removes its sibling-Apply exception. Retire dependent Protocol-invocation guidance unless a specifically named engine-entry case cannot be represented at a run binding site; any such exception must match across affected entries.

observing_check.positive: A local wrapper call moves to a run step with complete bindings and no residual Protocol Apply.
observing_check.negative: A primitive-owning technique invokes its raw tool and performs the reading without invoking another technique.

evidence.quote: A technique persists a session planning artifact by bare filename
Every planning artifact a workflow persists has a creation-guide resource with a `## Template` section and operative `## Rules` for filling it.

findings.problem: The broad guide requirement is narrowed by a literal bare-filename trigger. Token-named or resolved planning artifacts can miss Detect despite needing a guide under DP-28.
findings.witness: A producer declares artifact {component_name}-review.md and cites its canonical output id in Protocol, without a guide. The principle requires one; the entry's bare-filename predicate does not clearly reach it.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the opening Detect with: 'For each persisted planning artifact, whether its filename is literal, token-templated or resolved from a declared value, resolve the guide its producer cites. Flag a missing Template or operative fill Rules, or a competing Protocol layout.' Map artifact kinds or filename patterns to guides where one shape serves several names.

observing_check.positive: A token-named planning artifact without a guide receives a shape guide.
observing_check.negative: Several resolved filenames sharing one documented shape do not need separate guides per concrete name.

evidence.quote: Move the invariant into `## Rules` — the technique, the prompt resource, or the container `TECHNIQUE.md`.
A `## Rules` entry (or `rules.*` string) whose body is a citation, or a list of citations, to rules declared elsewhere, and the reader already receives those rules
Delete the enumeration and rely on the entry that already commands the inherited or bundled set.

findings.problem: Moving a redundant follow-delivered-rules phase to Rules creates the inherited-rule restatement AP-143 removes. AP-121 needs a delete branch before relocation.
findings.witness: A Protocol phase says to follow already delivered conduct rules throughout, with no work outcome. Moving it verbatim to Rules follows AP-121 but fails AP-143 because it adds no invariant.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace Fix with: 'Delete a standing duty already supplied by inherited or delivered rules. Move a unique cross-cutting invariant to its owning Rules surface, preserving every affected reader's reach. Keep work phases in Protocol.' Cite AP-143 for the redundant-citation branch.

observing_check.positive: A redundant follow-the-bundle phase is deleted without creating a Rules copy.
observing_check.negative: A unique domain invariant written as a phase moves to the proper Rules entry and remains delivered.
